task_description:
Set up a Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) research area, clean up folder naming, and reorganize a few bookmarks:

1) Create a new folder hierarchy:
   - Create a top-level folder named “Health & Wellness”.
   - Under it, create a folder named “Traditional Chinese Medicine”.
   - Under “Traditional Chinese Medicine”, create three subfolders: “Herbal Formulas”, “Acupuncture”, and “Dietary Therapy”.

2) Add the following TCM bookmarks (ensure valid URLs, avoid duplicates in their target folders, and include the descriptions). Also apply the specified tags, creating any missing tags first:
   - Title: “NCCIH: Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM)”
     URL: https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/traditional-chinese-medicine-what-you-need-to-know
     Folder: Health & Wellness > Traditional Chinese Medicine
     Description: “Overview of TCM from NIH NCCIH, including safety, evidence, and key practices.”
     Tags: TCM
   - Title: “WHO Acupuncture: Review and Analysis”
     URL: https://apps.who.int/iris/handle/10665/42414
     Folder: Health & Wellness > Traditional Chinese Medicine > Acupuncture
     Description: “WHO monograph summarizing clinical indications and evidence for acupuncture.”
     Tags: TCM, Acupuncture
   - Title: “Shen Nong: Chinese Herbal Materia Medica”
     URL: https://www.shen-nong.com/eng/herbal/
     Folder: Health & Wellness > Traditional Chinese Medicine > Herbal Formulas
     Description: “Herbal database covering properties, indications, and classical formulas.”
     Tags: TCM, Herbalism

3) Resolve folder name ambiguity:
   - Rename the top-level “Favorites” folder to “General Favorites”.
   - Rename the “Favorites” folder that is nested under “Programming Resources” to “Code Favorites”.

4) Reorganize and update existing bookmarks:
   - Move “Best Sushi Spots in Tokyo” into “Travel Ideas”.
   - Update its description to: “Curated list of top-rated sushi restaurants in Tokyo; moved to Travel Ideas for better organization.”
   - Move “Python Documentation” into “Code Favorites”.

Ensure all new URLs pass URL validation, do not create duplicate bookmarks within any folder, and preserve existing tags unless specified otherwise.
